paragraphs.notes: Continuation of a substituent definition begun on the preceding page (printed page 92); the page carries no label for it, so marker is null. It runs on into the R2a entry below and closes the definition list of the claim that immediately precedes claim 4. The zh field holds the verbatim German, since this is a German-language WO publication and not Chinese. Superscripts as printed: 8 and 9 on R in -P(=O)R8R9; 10 and 8 in -P(=O)OR10R8; 10 and 11 in -P(=O)OR10OR11; 2 on R in "durch R2 substituiert"; 2a on R in -R2a; 13 on R in -R13. Subscripts as printed: the 2 in every CH2, and the m, n and p in (CH2)m, (CH2)n and (O)p. Two spaces are printed after "eine der" before "Gruppen" and are kept. "Halogenalkinyl" is the German spelling for haloalkynyl throughout and is transcribed as printed. A small stray ink squiggle sits in the right margin beside the third and fourth lines of this paragraph; it is scan speckle, not a printed character.

paragraphs.notes: Superscript 2a on R; the 1, 2, 3 and 6 in every C1-C6, C2-C6 and C3-C6 are printed as subscripts. The label is set in a hanging indent, transcribed here as four spaces. The printed German mixes case within the same sentence: "Halogen-(C1-C6)-alkoxy" and "Halogen-(C2-C6)-alkenyloxy" lower case, but "Halogen-(C1-C6)-Alkyl" and "Halogen-(C1-C6)-Alkoxy" capitalised near the end; transcribed as printed. The closing verb "bedeuten" is plural and closes the whole definition list of this claim, not the R2a entry alone; translated literally as "denote" at the end of the sentence rather than moved to read naturally.
